notes.summary: Reconstructed middle-positive Borel multiplication and positivity at every generated-Psh ordinal stage: locally bounded u gives positive doubly closed D(uT). This proves separate-product positivity, not P21.3 independence.
notes.detailedSummary: The reconstruction uses compact middle-positive test decomposition, intrinsic signed coefficient Radon measures, and exterior-power matrix domination on finite moment presentations. A locally bounded final generated-Psh section bounds all decreasing predecessors below; upper semicontinuity supplies compact upper bounds. Fixed-measure convergence handles successors, ordinary locality handles limit ranks, and cardinal stabilization exhausts generated Psh. All original fields, degrees, singularities and generic multiplicities are retained. Reverse CPsh recognition and continuous predecessors are unnecessary. An arbitrary equal-curvature difference has not been given a two-sign generating construction.
notes.text:
Unverified research proof. Let K be any complete non-Archimedean field, including trivial valuation, and X good, separated, strict, boundaryless and pure of dimension n>=2. On every ordinary open W, let T be an ordinary middle-positive (p,p)-current, 0<=p<=n-1, satisfying d'T=d''T=0. Write D=d'd''. The proved statement is that every locally bounded real generated-Psh u has an ordinary Borel product uT and D(uT) is middle-positive and doubly closed.

The exact external ordinary-calculus inputs are CLD arXiv:1204.6277v2, 25 July 2025: compact neighbourhoods and ordinary analytic domains (11.1.7); calibrated analytic-domain compatibility (15.7.1–2); good Hausdorff implies local holomorphic/differential separation, with compact smooth cutoffs, localization and scalar density (15.2.2–9); compact symmetric tests are differences of compact middle-positive tests in this almost-good scope (6.5.2); positive scalar currents and positive complementary forms give unique Radon coefficient measures (7.2.8, 7.2.11); middle positivity is the signed positive-semidefinite matrix condition on exterior powers and is checked on tangent faces (1.2.6–7, 1.10.1); fixed-support chart topology is cellwise (7.1.1–3); compact moment images are polyhedral (only that part of 12.2.4); ordinary currents form a sheaf and have weakly continuous differentials with square-zero, anticommutation and duality identities (7.1.6–7, 7.7.1–5); and D(sT)=Ds wedge T for smooth s and doubly closed T (8.5.3–4). Positive smooth factors preserve middle positivity (7.2.7(b)). The original hypotheses provide this scope on every ordinary open. Neither the erroneous printed moment-dimension clause nor reverse Psh/CPsh recognition is used.

For a symmetric complementary compact test beta=eta1-eta2, define mu_beta=mu_eta1-mu_eta2 using its middle-positive decomposition. Competing decompositions agree against smooth compact scalars, hence against continuous compact scalars by density, so they define the same signed Radon measure. This establishes linearity. Density within the complement of supp beta shows the signed measure is supported in supp beta. Define <bT,beta>=integral b dmu_beta for locally bounded Borel b, using the symmetric projection for arbitrary tests.

To prove that this functional is an ordinary order-zero current, localize to rho f*a in one moment chart, with rho nonnegative compact smooth. Choose a compact analytic neighbourhood C of supp rho inside the chart, using a finite union of affinoids if needed. Its moment image has finitely many tangent faces. For complementary degree q=n-p, fix Euclidean Theta=sum dx_i' wedge dx_i''. Theta^q is positive definite on each qth exterior tangent space; both restrictions vanish on faces of dimension below q. Thus one constant c for this finite presentation gives c||a||_(P,0)Theta^q +/- a>=0 for every symmetric presented a. Positive coefficient measures imply |mu_(rho f*a)|<=c||a||_(P,0)mu_(rho f*Theta^q), hence
|<bT,rho f*a>|<=c||b||_(supp rho)||a||_(P,0)<T,rho f*Theta^q>.
For q=0 use the scalar bound. Chart topology and finite localization prove order-zero continuity without strongly-positive spanning. Coefficient-measure uniqueness also proves ordinary restriction compatibility and agreement with smooth multiplication.

If b_j decreases to b with common compact bounds, apply the fixed positive coefficient measures. For g_j=b_j-b decreasing to zero, 0<=g_j<=M, the sets E_j={g_j>=epsilon} decrease to the empty set. Finiteness gives mu(E_j)->0, while integral g_j<=epsilon mu(C)+M mu(E_j). Taking j to infinity and then epsilon to zero proves b_jT->bT weakly. Locally uniform nets against fixed T converge by the separate bound ||b_a-b||_C<T,eta1+eta2>. No bounded-pointwise-convergence assertion for arbitrary nets is made.

Reconstruct generated Psh from Definition 8.1.1 and Lemma 8.1.4: smooth positive-Hessian generators at rank zero, ordinary-local decreasing sequential limits at successors, and ordinary-local earlier-rank membership at limits. These are increasing sheaves. Upper semicontinuity follows at successors from {inf_j u_j<a}=union_j{u_j<a}, and is local at limits; finite sections are Borel. All open/section pairs form a set, so an equal-successor stage exists by cardinality. That stationary sheaf contains the generators and is decreasing-sequentially closed, hence is the minimal Psh sheaf. No extraneous integrability condition is inserted.

Induct simultaneously on every open and rank for locally bounded real final sections. Smooth u gives D(uT)=Du wedge T>=0. At a successor u_j decreases to u locally. Each predecessor is finite because u_j>=u and the stages allow no +infinity. The final u bounds every predecessor locally below; finite upper-semicontinuous u_j are locally bounded above. On each compact C there are fixed a,b with a<=u<=u_j<=u1<=b. Every predecessor therefore qualifies for induction even if discontinuous. Fixed-measure convergence gives D(u_jT)->D(uT), and positivity and symmetry pass to the limit. At limit ranks use earlier membership locally and the ordinary current sheaf. Stabilization proves all stages. Differential identities give both closedness equations. Scalar tests at p=n-1 and degree (n-1,n-1) tests at p=0 are included. The canonical calibration and generic lengths have not been changed.

Ordered differentiation by m locally bounded generated potentials is consequently positive and doubly closed for m<=n-p. If h and -h themselves are locally bounded generated Psh, D(hT) and its negative are positive; positive-test decomposition and symmetry force zero. The original assumptions on h=U-V have not supplied these two memberships.

Complete arguments and exact primary premises are in P21.3-argument.md and P21.3-paper.tex/PDF. Literal evidence, LF intervals and hashes are in P21.3-primary-evidence.md, premises.json and source-manifest.json. notes.summary: Mixed symmetry holds in the reconstructed argument for arbitrary original T with one continuous generated-Psh factor and one locally bounded generated-Psh factor. It does not settle signed curvature relations.
notes.detailedSummary: For p<=n-2, v continuous generated Psh and u locally bounded real generated Psh, D(uD(vT))=D(vD(uT)). The left successor limit uses fixed positive D(vT) coefficient measures; the right uses positive D(u_jT) and continuity of v. All sheafified ranks are treated. Adjacent swaps give permutation independence with at most one discontinuous factor. The signed continuous-difference identity still contains D(hT), which canonical D[h]=0 does not identify.
notes.text:
Unverified research proof using n1. Retain all original ambient hypotheses, ordinary middle positivity and canonical multiplicities. Suppose 0<=p<=n-2, u is locally bounded real generated Psh, and v is finite continuous generated Psh. Both inner differentiated currents are positive doubly closed by n1, so the products in D(uD(vT))=D(vD(uT)) are actual ordinary currents.

First reconstruct continuous multiplication on varying currents. If positive S_a->S weakly, positivity and symmetry pass on fixed tests. For compact symmetric beta=eta1-eta2, the masses <S_a,eta1+eta2> converge, hence are eventually bounded even for a net. Approximate continuous v uniformly on the compact union by smooth g, using a cutoff and the scalar density stated in n1. The error is at most epsilon<S_a,eta1+eta2>+|<S_a-S,g beta>|+epsilon<S,eta1+eta2>. First take the current limit for fixed g, then epsilon to zero. Thus vS_a->vS. Locally uniform varying continuous v_a also works by the additional bound ||v_a-v||_C<S_a,eta1+eta2>. This reconstructs CLD v2 Lemma 8.5.1 and its fixed-function net variant. It assumes neither a bound on all net indices nor a discontinuous multiplier.

A smooth doubly closed even-degree form gamma commutes with current differentiation by ordinary Leibniz duality. Also b(T wedge gamma)=(bT) wedge gamma for locally bounded Borel b whenever the currents involved are positive: their coefficient measures agree on smooth scalar tests and hence identically. The construction extends independently to finite differences of positive currents by uniqueness of signed coefficient measures.

Fix v,T and induct on u's sheafified rank, simultaneously on every ordinary subopen. For smooth u, Du is a positive smooth doubly closed form, and
D(uD(vT))=Du wedge D(vT)=D((vT) wedge Du)=D(v(T wedge Du))=D(vD(uT)).
This differentiates currents, not v as a smooth function.

At a successor take u_j decreasing to the locally bounded final u. The selection proved in n1 makes every predecessor locally bounded, with fixed compact bounds. The inductive equality holds for each u_j. Fixed-measure convergence for the fixed positive D(vT) gives u_jD(vT)->uD(vT). Separately, fixed-T convergence gives D(u_jT)->D(uT), all positive. Since v is continuous, the varying-current multiplication result gives vD(u_jT)->vD(uT). Weak continuity of D proves the equality. Limit ranks use earlier membership locally; ordinary locality and stabilization finish the proof. No continuous predecessors or CPsh recognition are used.

For m<=n-p factors with at most one discontinuous locally bounded generated factor, every adjacent swap has a continuous factor, so the theorem applies to its inner positive closed current. Outer operations preserve equality of positive currents. Adjacent transpositions give permutation independence. This does not interchange two arbitrary discontinuous factors.

For h=U-V with continuous generated U,V and continuous generated v, subtraction gives D(hD(vT))=D(vD(hT)); the right side is the difference of products with positive D(UT) and D(VT). Knowing D[h]=0 identifies D(h delta_X), not D(hT). The identity therefore retains the original unknown term.

Theorem 2 and its corollaries are in P21.3-argument.md and P21.3-paper.tex/PDF. Full CLD weak-multiplication evidence is LF10257–10281. The exact bound raw unit is sources/cld-weak-multiplier-bound.txt, hash 0448ea1b480496814c9d81b4a5443f7d6efbb05b91582305b117704008184860. notes.summary: New closure: D(vS) preserves continuous-pair compatibility for every locally bounded generated-Psh v, including discontinuous v. Arbitrary-current exhaustion remains unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: Orient mixed symmetry with the bounded differentiating v as the potentially discontinuous factor and the original U,V as continuous factors. Compatibility of S identifies the positive currents D(US)=D(VS), so their Borel products with v agree. This proves compatibility of D(vS) on every subopen. Smooth positive closed factors and weak positive limits also preserve compatibility. The resulting constructed-current class retains all original fields and ambient hypotheses, but no density theorem identifies it with arbitrary positive closed currents.
notes.text:
Unverified research proof using n1 and n2. Call a positive doubly closed S on W pair-compatible when every ordinary O subset W and every finite continuous generated-Psh U,V with D[U]=D[V] satisfy D(US)=D(VS). This is the original pair property for S, not a classification. Canonical delta_X is pair-compatible because U delta_X=[U]. It is positive by calibrated integration and doubly closed by boundaryless Stokes (CLD v2 15.7.1, 5.8.1–5, 7.7.4); these hypotheses apply to the original pure boundaryless space and its ordinary opens. Actual generic lengths are retained.

The new result is closure under D(vS) for any locally bounded real generated-Psh v, possibly discontinuous, when p<=n-2. On an arbitrary subopen carrying an admissible pair, n1 gives positive closed D(vS), D(US), D(VS). Apply n2 with potentially discontinuous u=v and continuous factor U, then with continuous factor V. It gives
D(UD(vS))=D(vD(US)), and D(VD(vS))=D(vD(VS)).
Compatibility of S identifies the positive currents D(US)=D(VS). Their actual Borel products with the same v agree by n1's intrinsic coefficient-measure construction. Therefore the desired products against D(vS) agree. The subopen was arbitrary, so this is an every-open property. No discontinuous multiplier passes through weak convergence on varying currents. This strengthens the supplied unreviewed proposal, which restricted the differentiating potential to be continuous.

Addition and nonnegative scaling preserve compatibility by linearity. Ordinary locality follows by restricting each pair and using the current sheaf. Weak positive nets preserve it: continuous U,V multiply S_a->S weakly by n2, then D passes to the limit. Positivity and both closedness equations pass on fixed tests. For a smooth middle-positive doubly closed decoration gamma, the wedge is positive closed and the smooth-factor identity gives D(h(S wedge gamma))=D(hS) wedge gamma=0. Require p+degree(gamma)<=n-1. None of these arguments needs global paracompactness or nontrivial valuation.

Starting from delta_X, these operations construct actual compatible currents, including ordered differentiation by several locally bounded discontinuous generated potentials. This does not prove permutation symmetry of two discontinuous factors or compatibility for discontinuous pairs.

The exact analytic exhaustion left unproved is: for every original K,X,p,W,T and x in W, find one ordinary neighbourhood N and a net of actual positive doubly closed degree-p currents on N, locally constructed from canonical delta_X by these operations, converging to T|N against all compact ordinary smooth tests and every analytic-unit moment refinement. Such an exhaustion would settle the original assertion by the proved weak closure and ordinary locality. No exhaustion follows from scalar smooth density, coefficient estimates, symmetry, or the definition of compatibility. A direct arbitrary-current preservation theorem, a valid fixed-neighbourhood construction for both signs of a general equal-curvature difference, or an admissible analytic counterexample is still needed.

Neither an ambient curvature restriction to arbitrary curves nor ascent under transcendental scalar extension is assumed. There is no asserted strong-current lift or product bridge. The granted strict real-PL and pure-curve results are not counted as universal coverage. This is a genuine closure theorem, rather than a formal annihilator restatement, but it leaves arbitrary-current quantification unresolved.

Theorem 3 and the unchanged target and missing analytic statement are in P21.3-argument.md and P21.3-paper.tex/PDF. status.json has exactly id,status,exact_result,proof_file,concrete_gaps, with status partial. Original inputs, source evidence, hashes, environment and build logs are preserved. Rerun bash reproduce.sh. Original P21.3 remains unresolved; candidate=false.

notes.summary: A fixed compact probability convolution kernel commuting with both split-torus monomial shears must be delta_0. This diagnoses one rigid regularization attempt; the original atom remains unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: Two actual analytic monomial automorphisms induce the shears A(x,y)=(x+y,y) and B(x,y)=(x,x+y). A single convolution kernel commuting with both pullbacks is invariant under both shears. Compact support and their iterates force its support to be zero. Transformed kernels and directed finite-presentation regularization are not excluded. Partition-of-unity gluing can separately lose closedness. Neither diagnostic supplies an admissible analytic counterexample. The paper builds and finite provenance checks pass, without mathematical acceptance.
notes.text:
Independent elementary diagnostic. Fix X=(G_m,Q2^2)^an, a good separated strict smooth boundaryless analytic surface. The monomial maps (z1,z2)->(z1z2,z2) and (z1,z2)->(z1,z1z2) have monomial inverses. In logarithmic coordinates they induce A(x,y)=(x+y,y) and B(x,y)=(x,x+y). CLD arXiv:1204.6277v2, 12.1.1–4 supplies the analytic-torus and functorial character/tropicalization setup; only these explicit maps are used.

Let mu be a compactly supported positive probability measure on R^2 and K_mu f(x)=integral f(x-z) dmu(z). Commutation with pullback by A, evaluated at zero for every compact smooth f, gives integral f(-Az) dmu(z)=integral f(-z) dmu(z), hence A_*mu=mu by uniqueness of Radon measures from smooth tests. Likewise B_*mu=mu. The compact support is invariant under these invertible shears. If (x,y) belongs to it, all A^k(x,y)=(x+ky,y) belong to it, so compactness forces y=0. Then all B^k(x,0)=(x,kx) belong to it, forcing x=0. Thus mu=delta_0. No nontrivial compact smooth probability mollifier has both fixed-kernel commutation properties.

This excludes only one unchanged scalar kernel. Coordinate-transformed kernels, kernels adapted to finite moment collections and directed compatible systems remain possible. The proposition proves no impossibility of analytic current regularization. It supplies no potentials, canonical curvature relation or defective product; the torus is already in established positive geometric ranges.

A separate Leibniz calculation shows why nonnegative partitions alone cannot glue closed regularizations: d'(sum rho_i R_i)=sum d'rho_i wedge R_i for closed R_i, and sum rho_i=1 does not cancel this expression without compatibility. On Euclidean R^2, R1=[1], R2=2[1], rho1=rho and rho2=1-rho with nonconstant 0<rho<1 give the positive but non-first-closed current [2-rho]. The differential rule is CLD v2 3.3.10–12 and 7.7.1–5. This is a failure of that gluing operation, not an analytic P21.3 counterexample.

The full original every-field, every-open, every-current continuous-pair assertion remains unproved in this work. No negative construction with separately admissible finite continuous generated-Psh U,V, upstairs canonical Hessian equality, an allowed positive doubly closed current and a detecting compact smooth test was obtained.
